s.autores.andrew-george.especialidad: Assyriologist, author of the standard critical edition of the Epic of Gilgamesh.
s.autores.andrew-george.aportaciones.0: He published the widely read translation of Gilgamesh for Penguin Classics (1999).
s.autores.andrew-george.aportaciones.1: He published the complete critical edition of the Babylonian version of Gilgamesh, with all the known tablets (2003).
s.autores.andrew-george.aportaciones.2: He edited the Babylonian topographical texts, which describe the city of Babylon and its temples.
s.autores.andrew-george.aportaciones.3: He has published unpublished texts from the Schøyen Collection, among them new literary fragments.
s.autores.andrew-george.postura: He reads Gilgamesh as a literary work about death, fame and human limits, transmitted and reworked over more than a thousand years.
s.autores.dalley.especialidad: Assyriologist, author of the most widely used English anthology of Akkadian myths.
s.autores.dalley.aportaciones.0: She translated the main Akkadian myths in a single volume: Atrahasis, Gilgamesh, Enuma Elish, Anzu, Erra, Etana, Adapa and the Descent of Ishtar.
s.autores.dalley.aportaciones.1: She argued that the Hanging Gardens were at Nineveh and not in Babylon.
s.autores.dalley.aportaciones.2: She has studied the presence of Mesopotamian cultures in the biblical and Hellenistic world.
s.autores.dalley.postura: She presents the myths in faithful translations with notes that point out gaps and doubtful readings, so that readers do not confuse the reconstruction with the original text.
s.autores.finkel.especialidad: Curator of the cuneiform tablets at the British Museum and a great popularizer.
s.autores.finkel.aportaciones.0: He published an Old Babylonian flood tablet that describes a circular ark (The Ark Before Noah, 2014).
s.autores.finkel.aportaciones.1: He reconstructed the rules of the Royal Game of Ur from a late tablet.
s.autores.finkel.aportaciones.2: He has worked on the Cyrus Cylinder and on Mesopotamian medicine and magic.
s.autores.finkel.postura: He shows how the flood stories were transmitted and modified in writing from one period to another, down to the biblical tradition.
s.autores.michalowski.especialidad: Sumerologist specializing in Sumerian literature, political history and the ideological use of texts.
s.autores.michalowski.aportaciones.0: He edited the Lamentation over the Destruction of Sumer and Ur (1989).
s.autores.michalowski.aportaciones.1: He edited the literary correspondence of the kings of Ur III (2011).
s.autores.michalowski.aportaciones.2: He has studied the Sumerian King List as an ideological text and not as a reliable chronicle.
s.autores.michalowski.postura: He insists that many "historical" and mythical texts are constructions of royal and school propaganda, composed or copied for political purposes.
s.autores.ossendrijver.institucion: Freie Universität Berlin (formerly Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin)
s.autores.ossendrijver.especialidad: Historian of ancient science, Assyriologist and astrophysicist, specialist in Babylonian mathematical astronomy.
s.autores.ossendrijver.aportaciones.0: He edited the procedure texts of Babylonian mathematical astronomy (2012).
s.autores.ossendrijver.aportaciones.1: He showed in Science (2016) that Babylonian astronomers calculated the motion of Jupiter by means of the area of a trapezoid, a geometric method thought to be much later.
s.autores.ossendrijver.aportaciones.2: He directs the ERC project ZODIAC on the birth of the zodiac and its spread.
s.autores.ossendrijver.postura: He shows that Babylonian astronomy was a sophisticated science of calculation about the visible planets, with no trace of a planet "Nibiru" like that of pseudoarchaeology.
s.autores.matuszak.institucion: University of Chicago (Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures)
s.autores.matuszak.especialidad: Sumerologist specializing in Sumerian literature, especially satirical texts, disputations and little-known myths.
s.autores.matuszak.aportaciones.0: She edited for the first time a Sumerian composition of invective against a woman, from the school tradition.
s.autores.matuszak.aportaciones.1: In 2025 she published and translated an unknown Sumerian myth from some 4,400 years ago, preserved on a tablet from Nippur, in which the fox acts as a trickster.
s.autores.matuszak.aportaciones.2: She has taught at Tübingen, SOAS (London) and Chicago.
s.autores.matuszak.postura: She pays attention to humor, parody and satire in Sumerian literature, aspects that show that not all texts were solemn or religious.
s.autores.enrique-jimenez.especialidad: Spanish Assyriologist, professor of Ancient Near Eastern Literatures and director of the Electronic Babylonian Library (eBL) project.
s.autores.enrique-jimenez.aportaciones.0: Since 2018 he has directed the eBL project, which digitizes and reconstructs Babylonian literature from thousands of fragments, mostly from the British Museum.
s.autores.enrique-jimenez.aportaciones.1: The eBL Fragmentarium, opened to the public in 2023, uses computational techniques to join fragments and has made it possible to identify new pieces of Gilgamesh and other works.
s.autores.enrique-jimenez.aportaciones.2: He edited the Babylonian disputation poems (2017).
s.autores.enrique-jimenez.postura: He considers that much of Babylonian literature remains fragmentary and that its reconstruction, now computer-assisted, is far from finished.
s.autores.konstantopoulos.especialidad: Assyriologist specializing in Mesopotamian religion, magic and literature, with a focus on demons and monsters.
s.autores.konstantopoulos.aportaciones.0: She studied the Sebettu ("the Seven"), a group at once divine and demonic, in a 2023 monograph.
s.autores.konstantopoulos.aportaciones.1: She has researched how Mesopotamian demons and monsters spread westward with the Assyrian campaigns.
s.autores.konstantopoulos.aportaciones.2: She works on imagined lands and mythical space, and on Enheduana and the myths of Inanna.
s.autores.konstantopoulos.postura: She analyzes demons and liminal beings as part of the Mesopotamian religious order, with functions that change according to the ritual or literary context.
s.autores.lara-peinado.especialidad: Historian of the ancient Near East and translator into Spanish of much of Mesopotamian literature.
s.autores.lara-peinado.aportaciones.0: He translated into Spanish the Epic of Gilgamesh, the Enuma Elish, Sumerian hymns and the Code of Hammurabi, among other texts.
s.autores.lara-peinado.aportaciones.1: He gathered the Sumerian and Akkadian myths in anthologies for Spanish-speaking readers.
s.autores.lara-peinado.aportaciones.2: He was professor of Ancient History at the Complutense from 1976 and received tribute volumes (UNED, 2011–2012; the journal Isimu, 2020).
s.autores.lara-peinado.postura: His work was above all popularization and translation, putting Mesopotamian texts within reach of the Spanish-speaking public.
s.autores.sanmartin.institucion: University of Barcelona (Department of Semitic Philology; IPOA)
s.autores.sanmartin.especialidad: Semitist philologist and Assyriologist, author of the standard Spanish translation of Gilgamesh.
s.autores.sanmartin.aportaciones.0: He translated directly from Akkadian and commented on the Epic of Gilgamesh (Trotta, 2005; revised edition 2018), considered the canonical version in Spanish.
s.autores.sanmartin.aportaciones.1: Coauthor with Gregorio del Olmo Lete of the standard dictionary of the Ugaritic language.
s.autores.sanmartin.aportaciones.2: He has headed the Assyriology section of the University Institute of Ancient Near Eastern Studies (IPOA).
s.autores.sanmartin.postura: He offers philological translations that clearly distinguish what is preserved on the tablets from what has been restored by the editor.
s.autores.jordi-vidal.especialidad: Historian of the ancient Near East (Ugarit, ancient warfare) and of orientalist historiography in Spain.
s.autores.jordi-vidal.aportaciones.0: He has studied society and war in Ugarit and in the ancient Near East.
s.autores.jordi-vidal.aportaciones.1: He directed a biographical dictionary of Spanish orientalists (2013).
s.autores.jordi-vidal.aportaciones.2: He researches the history of Assyriology and biblical archaeology in Spain, including the Franco era, and founded the journal Historiae.
s.autores.jordi-vidal.postura: He critically analyzes how modern political and religious contexts have conditioned the interpretation of the ancient Near East.
s.autores.millet-alba.institucion: University of Barcelona (Department of Semitic Philology; IPOA)
s.autores.millet-alba.especialidad: Assyriologist specializing in Amorite onomastics, Akkadian literature and comparative literature.
s.autores.millet-alba.aportaciones.0: With Lluís Feliu she translated the Epic of Gilgamesh into Catalan, an edition that received the Serra d'Or Critics' Award for translation (2023).
s.autores.millet-alba.aportaciones.1: She directs the University of Barcelona's archaeological mission at Tell Amarna (Syria).
s.autores.millet-alba.aportaciones.2: She teaches Akkadian in the master's program in Assyriology and is editorial secretary of the journal Aula Orientalis.
s.autores.millet-alba.postura: She combines Akkadian philology and comparative literature to place Gilgamesh and other texts within the world literary tradition.
s.autores.heiser.institucion: Logos Bible Software (PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison)
s.autores.heiser.especialidad: Biblical scholar trained in ancient Semitic languages (including Akkadian), not an Assyriologist; critic of Zecharia Sitchin.
s.autores.heiser.aportaciones.0: He maintained the website Sitchin Is Wrong, where he checked Sitchin's claims against the cuneiform texts and academic dictionaries.
s.autores.heiser.aportaciones.1: He showed that the Mesopotamian texts do not describe a planet Nibiru with a 3,600-year cycle, nor the Anunnaki as extraterrestrials.
s.autores.heiser.aportaciones.2: He criticized the reading of the seal VA 243 as a map of the solar system.
s.autores.heiser.postura: His criticism was philological, although his own interpretation started from a Christian theological perspective on the supernatural in the Bible, something worth bearing in mind.
s.hitos.1802-0.evento: Georg Friedrich Grotefend proposes the first correct readings of Old Persian cuneiform signs
s.hitos.1835-0.evento: Henry Rawlinson begins copying the trilingual Behistun inscription (work he completes around 1847)
s.hitos.1845-0.evento: Austen Henry Layard begins the excavations at Nimrud; soon afterward he excavates Nineveh (Kuyunjik)
s.hitos.1853-0.evento: Hormuzd Rassam discovers at Nineveh the North Palace of Ashurbanipal, with thousands of tablets from his library
s.hitos.1857-0.evento: Royal Asiatic Society test: Rawlinson, Hincks, Oppert and Talbot separately translate the same inscription and their versions agree in essentials
s.hitos.1872-0.evento: George Smith presents the Babylonian flood story from Tablet XI of Gilgamesh before the Society of Biblical Archaeology
s.hitos.1877-0.evento: Ernest de Sarzec begins excavating Tello (Girsu): the finds confirm the existence of the Sumerians
s.hitos.1889-0.evento: The University of Pennsylvania begins the excavations at Nippur, the source of much of the known Sumerian literature
s.hitos.1921-0.evento: The Chicago Assyrian Dictionary is launched in Chicago; it was completed in 26 volumes in 2010
s.hitos.1944-0.evento: Samuel Noah Kramer publishes Sumerian Mythology, the first synthesis of the Sumerian myths
s.hitos.1969-0.evento: W. G. Lambert and A. R. Millard publish the edition of Atrahasis
s.hitos.1997-0.evento: The Electronic Text Corpus of Sumerian Literature (ETCSL), directed by Jeremy Black, begins at Oxford
s.hitos.2003-0.evento: Andrew George publishes the complete critical edition of the Babylonian Epic of Gilgamesh
s.hitos.2016-0.evento: Mathieu Ossendrijver shows in Science the use of geometric methods in Babylonian astronomy to calculate the motion of Jupiter
s.hitos.2018-0.evento: Enrique Jiménez launches the Electronic Babylonian Library project at LMU Munich; its Fragmentarium opens to the public in 2023
